what_its_for: Pimecrolimus is a cream used to treat mild to moderate eczema (atopic dermatitis). It helps reduce redness, itching, and irritation on your skin. It is usually used when other eczema treatments have not worked or cannot be used. It is approved for adults and children 2 years of age and older.
how_to_take: Apply a thin layer of the cream to the affected areas of your skin twice a day. Gently rub it in until it disappears. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream, unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or wraps unless your doctor tells you to. You can use moisturizers along with this cream — apply them after the pimecrolimus cream.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area twice daily (morning and evening). Use only the smallest amount needed to cover the affected area. Only apply it to areas of skin that are affected by eczema — do not put it on normal, healthy skin. Do not use it inside your nose, mouth, or eyes.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Do not freeze the cream. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medication out of reach of children. Do not store it in the bathroom where it could be exposed to heat and moisture.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Avoid sunbathing, tanning beds, and sunlamps while using this medication, as it may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight — use sunscreen and protective clothing when going outdoors. Avoid using this cream on infected skin unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not wrap or cover treated skin tightly. Avoid contact with people who have chickenpox, shingles, or other skin infections while using this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice any of the following: skin infections (signs include increased redness, warmth, swelling, oozing, or pain), swollen lymph nodes, unusual skin growths or changes, signs of an allergic reaction (hives, difficulty breathing, swelling of face or throat), your eczema is getting worse instead of better after several weeks of use, or you develop chickenpox or shingles. Call your doctor right away if you have any serious side effects.
when_it_works: Many people begin to notice improvement in their symptoms, such as reduced itching and redness, within the first 1 to 2 weeks of use. Some people may see results sooner. Continue using the cream as directed by your doctor even if your symptoms improve. If there is no improvement after 6 weeks of treatment, contact your doctor — a different treatment may be needed.
special_populations: Children: This medication is approved for children 2 years of age and older, but should not be used in children under 2 years old. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this cream if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as there is limited information about its safety in these situations. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed, but elderly patients should still consult their doctor before use. People with weakened immune systems: Use with caution — speak with your doctor, as this medication affects the immune response in the skin.
